item.title: The Beginner's Guide to Neural Networks
item.content:encoded: This beginner-friendly guide explains the core mechanics of neural networks, focusing on weights, biases, gradient descent, and batch processing. Through analogies, simple Python examples, and practical learning advice, it aims to help new AI learners build an intuitive understanding of how neural networks learn and why foundational mathematics is essential.

item.title: Building User-Aware AI Agents with MCP and Serverless
item.content:encoded: Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets AI discover and use new tools on the fly. Each MCP server becomes a domain-specific intelligence hub that can serve multiple agents while maintaining its own security and business logic.

item.title: How Your Agents Produce Code Is More Valuable Than the Code Itself
item.content:encoded: When you work with agents, the data from your interactions becomes the prime commodity — the raw material for building the next iteration and training the next generation of agents to do the job more accurately and more efficiently. Even the mistakes and errors are valuable learning opportunities. It is no coincidence that the flagship coding agents came from the two leading model labs, and those same labs shipped the most advanced models right after. Your interaction with your agents is unique. It is your fingerprint, your mold — your primary IP. And to own it means holding full control over both its interface and its infrastructure.

item.title: Most AI Agents Aren't Really Agents At All
item.content:encoded: Drawing on the Critique of Agent Model paper, this article argues that many modern AI agents are better described as agentic workflows than genuinely agentive systems. It explores the distinction through concepts like persistent goals, adaptive identity, self-regulation, world models, and continuous learning, offering a more rigorous framework for evaluating autonomous AI.

item.content:encoded: The RWA market may have surpassed **$50 billion** in tokenized assets, but that doesn't mean institutional capital has arrived. Tokenization solved asset representation, not capital deployment. Institutions still face fragmented wallet access, shallow liquidity, limited yield opportunities, and settlement risks that make large-scale allocation unattractive. The next phase of RWA growth depends less on creating more tokenized assets and more on building the infrastructure that lets capital move efficiently. Until distribution, liquidity, native stablecoin settlement, and institutional-grade access improve, the industry's trillion-dollar ambitions will remain more narrative than reality.

item.title: I Built a PC Monitor That Learns Your Hardware
item.content:encoded:

But your machine isn't in any table: silicon lottery, component aging, ambient temperature, and load composition mean a generic profile describes a computer you don't own. The fix is statistics on YOUR history, not the manufacturer's spec — median + MAD with Nelson Rules (the same Statistical Process Control factories use), workload-bucketed thermal baselines via Welford's algorithm, all running locally and offline with zero telemetry. A PSU rail sagging to 11.7V is "in spec" to a threshold but a 5-sigma anomaly against your own learned 11.95-12.05V norm — caught months before failure. Not a chatbot bolted on. Real statistics that don't hallucinate. It's working open-source code in PC Workman v1.7.9, built solo over 11 months between physical-labor shifts.

item.title: Stop Wasting API Calls & Implement the Tab Leader Pattern Instead
item.content:encoded:
The Tab Leader Pattern eliminates redundant API polling across multiple browser tabs. Only one tab handles data fetching while all others benefit from shared cache updates through localStorage and the BroadcastChannel API. This pattern reduces API calls by 80-90% while improving data consistency.
